commits.author: noogalabs
commits.subject: fix(pty): rotate stdout.log at 50 MB to prevent file-cache pressure (#175)
commits.body:
Long-running agent sessions accumulate stdout.log unboundedly. On macOS
the OS file cache fills up and log writes degrade around 50-100 MB.

Adds a lightweight rotation: when the log exceeds 50 MB on the next
push(), rename the file to stdout.log.1 (silently discarding any prior
.1), then continue appending to a fresh stdout.log.

Bug fixed in same change: the original statSync call was inside the same
try block as appendFileSync, so an ENOENT on first write (file doesn't
exist yet) would silently swallow the append. Fixed by wrapping the
rotation check in its own inner try/catch so a missing file skips
rotation but still reaches appendFileSync.

Co-authored-by: David Hunter <davidhunter@Davids-Mac-mini.local>
Co-authored-by: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.author: noogalabs
commits.subject: fix(daemon): skip type=disabled cron entries in gap detector and verification (#176)
commits.body:
Cron entries with type=disabled in config.json were passing through both
scheduleGapDetection() and scheduleCronVerification() filter expressions,
which only excluded type=once. This caused gap-nudge messages to fire every
10 minutes for intentionally disabled crons.

Fix: add c.type !== 'disabled' to both filter sites.
Also adds 'disabled' to the CronEntry type union and two regression tests.

commits.author: James Goldbach
commits.subject: fix(daemon): stagger gap nudges + guard duplicate cron verification (issue #182) (#183)
commits.body:
Two bugs that compound into restart storms when multiple crons are stale
simultaneously after a daemon restart:

1. runGapDetectionLoop fired all stale-cron nudges back-to-back in a
   tight loop. N simultaneous nudges → N rapid Claude turns → context
   spike → ctx-watchdog force-restart → storm. Fix: 30s sleep between
   nudge injections so the agent settles between turns.

2. verifyCronsAfterIdle timed out after 10min if the agent was busy
   (processing the nudge burst), silently dropping the verification.
   Fix: extend maxWaitMs to 30min. Also add cronVerificationPending
   guard so rapid --continue restarts don't stack duplicate waiters.

commits.author: James Goldbach
commits.subject: fix(daemon): pre-arm .force-fresh at Tier 2 handoff to break --continue loop (#194)
commits.body:
When context hits the handoff threshold, the daemon injects a handoff
prompt and gives the agent 5min to cooperate. If the agent exhausts
context before calling hard-restart, the session exits with code 0 and
shouldContinue() returns true — restarting in --continue mode at the
same high context level, re-triggering the watchdog immediately, and
creating a restart storm.

Fix: write .force-fresh the moment the handoff prompt is injected. This
ensures the next restart is always a fresh session regardless of whether
the agent cooperates or context exhausts naturally. If the agent does
call hard-restart, it also writes .force-fresh — no double effect.

Closes the --continue context thrashing loop observed in sentinel/donna
(77% → 78% → 78% → 79% → 81% rapid cycle, Apr 20 2026).

Co-authored-by: Boris <boris@cortextos.ai>
Co-authored-by: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.author: James Goldbach
commits.subject: fix(daemon): guard PTY write callbacks against null to prevent daemon crash (#196)
commits.body:
Three injectMessage call sites passed `(data) => this.pty!.write(data)` as
the write callback. inject.ts fires a 300ms delayed setTimeout for the Enter
keypress — if the agent's PTY is destroyed in that window, the callback throws
TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'write'), which propagates
as an unhandled exception and crashes the daemon process.

PM2 auto-restarts the daemon on crash, which stops and restarts every agent
simultaneously. With agents already at high context (continue mode), this
triggers the context-thrashing loop, causing the rapid restart storm seen
on 2026-04-20 (226 daemon crashes in ~15 minutes).

Fix: replace `this.pty!.write` with `this.pty?.write` at all three call sites
(injectMessage, gap nudge injection, cron verification injection). The optional
chain silently no-ops if the PTY is gone — the Enter keypress is lost but the
daemon stays alive.

Co-authored-by: Boris <boris@cortextos.ai>
Co-authored-by: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.author: James Goldbach
commits.subject: fix(daemon): pass handoff doc on Tier 3 force-restart + elevate pickup message priority (#197)
commits.body:
- forceContextRestart() now scans memory/handoffs/ for a doc written
  in the last 15 minutes before calling hardRestart(). If found,
  writes .handoff-doc-path so the new session starts with full handoff
  context even when Tier 3 cuts the agent short.

- handoffUxOverride in buildStartPrompt() now marks the pickup Telegram
  message as CRITICAL and orders it BEFORE cron restoration and heartbeat,
  preventing it from being buried in the boot sequence.

commits.author: Boris
commits.subject: fix(daemon): make handoff pickup message a concrete tool call, not prose instruction
commits.body:
The previous instruction said 'send ONE brief conversational Telegram message'
but agents interpreted this as generating text output rather than actually
calling cortextos bus send-telegram. Changed to: 'your VERY FIRST tool call
MUST be a Bash call running: cortextos bus send-telegram ...'

Diagnosed via nick's stdout.log: he composed the right pickup text but never
called send-telegram. The bus command was never executed.
